conviction_note: An annual print where the FY27 guide is the line: the Q4 bar ($0.75) sits in the upper part of what the reaffirmed FY26 guide implies ($0.68-0.78 cc), so the quarter is mostly told; the lean is mildly positive (record wins $1.6B YTD, 98% retention, Nexus sites ramping into FY27, a stock de-rated 12-14% off its post-Q3 high on AI-theme selling, peers' NA sports/leisure strong) against a Texas data-center permitting overhang and FY27 startup-cost margin risk, so p_up 55 on a 7% absolute move gives +0.7; findings sum +1.4, larger than the scaled number because the scaled number carries the sign uncertainty and the findings do not.
bar: Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS $0.75 (Earnings Whispers, https://finviz.com/news/418744/aramark-must-prove-record-wins-and-nexus-ramp-can-lift-profits-not-just-revenue, 2026-11-08; AAII also $0.75, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/531546-what-you-need-to-know-about-aramarks-q4-earnings); Chartmill shows $0.77 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/0AK.DE/estimates). Revenue bar disputed: ~$5.27B (EW) vs $5.41B (Chartmill). Company guide: FY26 adj EPS +20-25% cc on FY25 $1.82 = $2.18-2.28; YTD cc $1.50 (Q3 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001584509/000158450926000118/ex991armkq3fy2026.htm) so implied Q4 cc $0.68-0.78. Note EW's 'FY26 guidance $2.27-2.36' and 'year-ago $0.64' are computed off a wrong base (FY25 Q4 adj EPS was $0.57 per the Q4 FY25 release coverage). FY27 consensus is unsourced (stale ranges $2.44-3.07), so the guide bar is unknown.
positioning_check: Short interest ~2.9% of shares outstanding, 2.53 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30 via https://equibles.com/stocks/armk/shortinterest, sweep row); Fintel undated 4.06% of float / 5.7 days. Not crowded. Skew_25d is null in the baseline (no directional statement from options); put/call OI 0.03 on a thin front chain with 67% ATM spread, so the 5.12% event-implied move is indicative only. Price: $61 on 2026-08-13 (COO sales at $60.35-61.50), $52.42 on 2026-10-22 after a -5.9% day on AI-spending worries, $50.28 on 2026-11-06, $53.30 at seal (5d +1.4%, 20d -3.6%, -14.6% from 52w high). Consensus PT $68.5 (Simply Wall St, 2026-10-27).

findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY26 guide (adj EPS +20-25% cc on FY25 $1.82 = $2.18-2.28; YTD cc $1.50) implies Q4 adj EPS of $0.68-0.78 cc and Q4 AOI of $326-375M cc against $289M a year ago (FY25 AOI 692.6+289 = $981.6M; YTD FY26 AOI cc $773.4M); the $0.75 consensus sits ~70% up that range, and the year-ago Q4 carried ~$25M of extra incentive comp, an easy comp management said would see AOI growth and margin expansion 'accelerate' in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 (2025-11-17): adj EPS $0.57 vs ~$0.65 consensus, on $25M incentive comp, stock -5.23%. Q3 FY26 (2026-08-11) AOI +13% (+21% ex-calendar), EPS +30%, raised organic guide: +8.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the quarter lands inside a guide the company reaffirmed, and consensus already sits in the upper half. What is not on the wire is the arithmetic: EW's preview says FY consensus $2.24 is below a '$2.27-2.36' guide, which is a base error; on the correct base consensus is near the top of guide, so the quarter is not an easy beat. If the market believed a top-end print were likely, the stock would not be 14% under its post-Q3 level.
findings.independence: Prior-year Q4 base and incentive comp: https://www.mychesco.com/a/news/regional/aramark-posts-higher-revenue-and-strong-cash-flow-in-fiscal-2025/ (AOI $289M, ~$25M incentive comp). Q4 acceleration language: https://www.mychesco.com/a/news/regional/aramark-raises-sales-outlook-as-ai-data-center-business-grows/ (2026-08-24). Shares the Q3 8-K with findings 3 and 7.

findings.finding: Aramark Nexus (AI data-center workforce hospitality) is ramping into FY27: the first Texas hyperscaler site's scope rose ~40% to ~$140M a year, a second ~$160M site is mobilizing, eight sites are assigned, management sized the three active sites at $400-500M annualized revenue (~2% of a ~$20B base) ramping through FY27-28 at above-average, cost-reimbursable margins, plus a separate colocation-provider deal (Wyoming, Texas) mobilizing in 1H FY27 — a first FY27 guide that carries this is above anything the company has guided before.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nexus launch (2026-04-22) and the Q2 print (2026-05-12) +8.64%; Q3 print with the raised organic guide citing the hyperscaler +8.54%. The stock has traded as an AI-theme beneficiary since (-5.9% on 2026-10-22 on AI-spend worries).
findings.why_not_priced: The site values are public, but no FY27 number containing them exists; the stock gave back the Q3 gain on AI-capex fear, so the market is pricing doubt about the ramp, not the ramp. If it were priced the stock would sit near the $61 post-Q3 level, not $53.
findings.independence: Company 8-K exhibit (first site operating, second mobilizing, raised organic outlook reflecting hyperscaler): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001584509/000158450926000118/ex991armkq3fy2026.htm; colocation deal: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8974349/aramark-nexus-selected-by-ai-data-center-colocation-leader-to-provide-premium-hospitality-services-to-workforce-communities. Same line as finding 3 (Texas), opposite sign; both can be true (current sites ramping, future sites at regulatory risk).

findings.finding: Texas, where Aramark's first hyperscaler site and part of the colocation deal sit, has tightened on data centers since Aramark last spoke: Abbott ordered a PUCT/ERCOT audit of every data center in the interconnection queue on 2026-08-03, told TCEQ to pause data-center permits until the audit ends on 2026-09-21, and governor-elect Hinojosa (takes office 2027-01-19) pledged on ~2026-11-05 to halt new approvals; Hill County passed a one-year moratorium. This puts the 'additional sites' part of the FY27 Nexus pipeline at risk and is expected to be asked on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has addressed it. The stock fell 5.9% on 2026-10-22 on AI-spending worries, a day peers held up (Weiss), showing the theme moves it.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the AI-theme sell-off. What is not priced is a company-specific answer: the sites in operation are construction-phase workforce camps, and EW reports management says the audit risk sits with the hyperscaler; if the FY27 guide shades Nexus timing, that is new. Proxy: no document ties Aramark's sites to the paused permits.
findings.independence: EW preview flags the Texas moratorium/audit as an expected call topic: https://finviz.com/news/418744/aramark-must-prove-record-wins-and-nexus-ramp-can-lift-profits-not-just-revenue; Hill County: https://www.businessreport.com/article/why-a-texas-county-just-hit-the-brakes-on-data-center-development. Macro-to-company proxy, not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: Record new business ($1.6B+ YTD gross new wins, +51%) and ~98% retention at Q3, with the UPHS seven-hospital contract (the second-largest in company history, started early 2026) and new higher-ed, destinations and healthcare accounts that the CFO said ramp further in FY27, set up an FY27 organic growth guide at or above FY26's 9-10% (Q3 underlying run-rate cited at 10-11%); the counterweight, also cited by EW, is startup costs from a record mobilization that could cap the FY27 margin step, so the size is net of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First guide for FY26 (2025-11-17: organic 7-9%, AOI +12-17%, EPS +20-25%) came with a Q4 EPS miss and -5.23%; raised organic guides in Q2/Q3 FY26 were bought +8.6%/+8.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The win figures are on the wire; the FY27 guide that converts them is not, and FY27 consensus could not be sourced to a current number (stale $2.44-3.07 range), so the Street's bar is soft. If the market expected an accelerating FY27 guide the stock would not have de-rated 14% since the last print.
findings.independence: Peer evidence of share shift: Sodexo NA FY26 Education -5.1% and B&A -9.7% on contract losses (https://www.webdisclosure.com/press-release/sodexo-fiscal-2026-results-organic-growth-above-guidance-fiscal-2027-outlook-confirmed-JMiOXuH4pIc, 2026-10-23). UPHS: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35319825/aramark-healthcare-and-university-of-pennsylvania-health-system-announce-systemwide-partnership. Shares the Q3 8-K with finding 1.

findings.finding: Peers reporting after Aramark's last call point to a healthy Q4 (Jul-Sep) in sports, leisure and North American contract catering: Sodexo (2026-10-23) said Q4 activity was stronger than anticipated, Sodexo Live! NA +7.3% for FY26 on 'high attendance and strong consumer spending'; Compass (2026-07-21) NA organic +7.5% in Q3 with a raised profit guide; MLB 2026 attendance rose 0.5% to ~71.75M, a fourth straight gain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history; Sports & Entertainment is one of several US businesses and has not been named as the line a reaction turned on.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy evidence in other companies' releases and a league attendance series; previews of ARMK do not cite them. Small because the sports leg is a minority of FSS US and the quarter is already guided.
findings.independence: Compass Q3: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/CPG/q3-trading-update-szxha0db0ulx84g.html; MLB attendance: https://www.ticketnews.com/2026/10/mlb-attendance-grows-for-fourth-straight-year-to-highest-level-since-2017/. Proxy, not confirmed by Aramark.

findings.finding: The stock goes in de-rated: from ~$61 on 2026-08-13 to $50.28 on 2026-11-06 and $53.30 at seal (-14.6% from the 52w high), with the 2026-10-22 -5.9% day attributed to market-wide AI-spending worries rather than company news, while estimates rose (Zacks Rank #2 on a higher full-year estimate, 2026-10-27) and short interest is only ~3%: the bar into the guide is lower than at the last two prints, which were both bought.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last three prints up (+5.57, +8.64, +8.54); 4 of 7 up overall with a median absolute move of 8.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown itself is in the price by definition; what it changes is the hurdle for the guide. The same Weiss note cites a forward P/E of ~39, so the de-rating is from a rich level and this is sized small.

findings.finding: Leverage was 3.5x at Q3 against a reaffirmed sub-3.0x year-end target, with a large Q4 cash inflow guided (Collegiate, Sports); last year the same seasonality took leverage from 4.0x at Q3 to 3.25x at year-end, so reaching <3.0x is plausible and would clear management's stated precondition for larger buybacks (YTD repurchases only $67M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY25 year-end leverage at a near-20-year low (3.25x) coincided with a -5.23% reaction driven by the EPS miss; no clean reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The target is public; a capital-return step-up (buyback authorization or accelerated repurchase) tied to hitting it is not announced. Small.
findings.independence: FY25 leverage walk: https://www.mychesco.com/a/news/regional/aramark-posts-higher-revenue-and-strong-cash-flow-in-fiscal-2025/. Shares the Q3 8-K with findings 1 and 4.

findings.finding: Last year's Q4 missed by ~$0.08 because of ~$25M of incentive compensation tied to record net new business; FY26 net new business is again a record (+51% gross wins YTD), so a similar Q4 accrual is possible, though it is now in the base and the guide was reaffirmed knowing the wins.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-17: Q4 adj EPS $0.57 vs $0.65 consensus on the incentive accrual, stock -5.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews (EW) do not mention it and EW quotes the year-ago Q4 as $0.64, which suggests the accrual's history is not in its model. Inside guidance, so sized small.
findings.independence: Q4 FY25 miss vs $0.65: https://benzinga.com/z/48899294 (from search snippet; the release itself is the 8-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001584509/000158450925000214/ex991armkq4fy2025.htm). Shares the record-wins fact with finding 4, opposite effect (cost now, revenue later).

findings.finding: The COO of U.S. Food & Facilities, Marc Bruno, exercised 210k options (one tranche expiring 2026-11-18) on 2026-08-13 and sold ~70.6k shares at $60.35-61.50, not marked as a 10b5-1 plan; no other open-market insider selling since, and the recurring Form 4 clusters (Sep 10, Oct 6, Nov 12) are the same six filers on a monthly cadence.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August and mostly driven by expiring options; sized near zero.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with; the findings lean mildly positive against a negative 20-day run-up and a 14% drawdown since the last print, which is a lower bar rather than a signal, and the AI-theme beta that drove the drawdown can drive the reaction either way.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside guidance): the Q4-guide arithmetic finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1 and the incentive-comp repeat risk from -0.4 to -0.2, both land inside a reaffirmed guide
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Nexus ramp cut from +1.0 to +0.7, record wins/FY27 from +0.8 to +0.6, since both facts are on the wire and only the guide is new
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): Texas permitting overhang cut from -0.7 to -0.4 (no document ties Aramark's sites to it), peer read-through from +0.3 to +0.2
Rule 5 (drawdown is not a cause by itself): positioning cut from +0.4 to +0.3; it has a cause (AI-spend selling) so it stays filed

Rule 3 (read the set): Nexus (+) and Texas (-) kept as two findings because both can be true; bar print_vs_bar lowered from +1.5 to +1.0 after confirming consensus sits near the top of the implied range
